title: GS-bypass regression gate (NATIVE_QUAD + NATIVE_TRI_DEPTH equivalence + path-activation assertion)
purpose: Render three stripe-passes per frame -- PASS 1 OP_QUADS SMOOTH (top half, 12 cells, engages NATIVE_QUAD), PASS 2 OP_TRIANGLES SMOOTH (bottom half rows 0-1, 8 cells, engages NATIVE_TRI_DEPTH smooth path), PASS 3 OP_TRIANGLES FLAT FLAT_SHADE_OP=VERTEX_FIRST (bottom half row 2, 4 cells, engages NATIVE_TRI_DEPTH first-provoking path with TL=EXPECTED + TR/BR/BL=BLACK distractors). Math-derived expected output is the same 4x3 saturated 0/255 RGB grid in both halves: any divergence catches NATIVE_QUAD CPU-triangulation bugs, smooth interpolation bugs, per-fragment depth-path leakage into color, or NATIVE_TRI_DEPTH's first-provoking selection picking the wrong vertex. Pixel-equivalence alone cannot prove the bypass engaged -- a silent GS fallback also produces correct pixels -- so the harness also enforces required_counters_min on NATIVE_QUAD_DRAW + the per-stripe-specific NATIVE_TRI_DEPTH_DRAW_SMOOTH and NATIVE_TRI_DEPTH_DRAW_FLAT_FIRST counters (the aggregate counters are NOT asserted because one pass alone would satisfy them and mask a regression in the other -- Codex 2026-05-20 finding). Counter thresholds (>=100 each) sit well below the ~300 draws-per-counter-per-renderer this XBE emits over its 300-frame render loop. FLAT-shaded OP_QUADS is intentionally NOT tested here -- it exposed a real Metal renderer gap (no GS, no manual CPU flat-color propagation) during initial validation; that coverage is deferred to a follow-up XBE plus a tracked renderer slice. Pure 0/255 RGB so byte-exact across renderers regardless of display gamma. compare_overrides are tightened below one-cell size (cells are 160x80 = 4.17% of frame; max_changed_pct=3.5 + min_signal_match_pct=97.0 leaves ~1.5%/~1.16% headroom above the measured ~2% boundary-AA budget so a whole-cell regression cannot pass -- Codex 2026-05-20 evening, late changes-mode finding #1).
